hypothesis: An LLM self-merge reviewer's correctness is bounded by the context it receives: a truncated git diff makes it over-reject (it cannot verify internal consistency or intent, so it defaults to REQUEST_CHANGES on anything unverifiable), while the full post-change file content + the linked-issue intent makes it both fair AND able to catch real internal contradictions.

plan.description: Feed reviewer_b (council_emit.py) the linked-issue title/body (authorized intent) + the full post-change content of each changed file (<=10) + the diff, instead of only a truncated diff. Calibrate the prompt to judge the change itself (pre-authorized by the issue) and NOT block on facts unverifiable from the provided material (e.g. whether a referenced PR exists). Make verdict parsing read the explicit final 'Verdict:' line rather than a loose substring.
plan.success_criteria: On a clean, internally-consistent low-risk change the council reaches APPROVE stably (>=4/5 samples); on a change with a real internal contradiction the council REJECTs and names the contradiction.
risks: A single LLM sample is non-deterministic on borderline changes
Full-file context costs more tokens per review
gh api --jq .content returns raw base64, not JSON

do.action_taken: Shipped in PR #392: build_review_context (issue body + full changed-file content via fetch_file_at_ref reading raw base64 directly + diff), prompt calibration (judge the change; don't block on unverifiable repo-external facts; explicit INTERNAL CONSISTENCY check), and parse_verdict reading the final Verdict line.

check.evidence: With full-file context the council caught THREE genuine internal contradictions in the dogfood doc (#391) and withheld merge each time; once the doc was actually consistent reviewer_b was 5/5 APPROVE and the self-merge fired (master 9c04482). The diff-only version had over-rejected the same clean change.

act.rationale: Full-file + intent context is now the council default on master. OPEN FOLLOW-UP (next PDCA if borderline flakiness appears operationally): a single LLM reviewer was stable on clean changes here, but the gate is a hard binary veto on one sample. If borderline PRs prove flaky across cycles, upgrade reviewer_b to an N-sample majority (or treat it as advisory below a confidence band) so non-determinism cannot block a correct change or pass a bad one. Monitor via state/oversight/afk-harvest-*.json and state/council/ verdicts.
